title: poot benchmark result record
description: One record per (framework, model, precision, scenario) cell. The harness writes one JSON object per line into results.jsonl. Timing fields come from the runner; memory fields come from the harness external sampler; the env block is written once per run into env.json (not repeated per row). Which binary, on which backend, adapter and device, produced a row is on the row itself: a poot row names its build (build_sha, build_profile, build_features, rustc_version), the adapter and driver the executor reported, the digest of the checkpoint it loaded and the dtype its weights are stored in (precision); an external tool row names its framework_version.

deviceTime.description: The device's own time for a profiled window (poot --profile): null when not profiled, `unknown` when the device reports none (ROCm, an untimed device), else measured milliseconds with at least one measure present. Never a zero standing for unknown.

nonnegativePercentiles.description: The median and observed range of the samples. p90 and p99 appear only from 20 samples on (harness/result_contract.py TAIL_PERCENTILE_MIN_SAMPLES), where they estimate a tail instead of interpolating between a handful of points.

positivePercentiles.description: As nonnegativePercentiles, for a strictly positive quantity.

framework_version.description: Resolved version of the engine (cargo pkg version / pip version / llama.cpp git tag).

precision.description: Precision actually run for this cell (e.g. f32, bf16, fp16, gptq-int4, awq-int4, mxfp4, q4_k_m).

status.description: ok = measured; unsupported = framework cannot run this model/precision (see reason); error = run failed (see reason).

reason.description: Required when status is 'unsupported' or 'error': the explicit reason / error message. For 'unsupported' it is the refusal exactly as the tool reports it.

build_sha.description: The git sha the runner binary was built from, embedded at build time and reported by the runner ('-dirty' when the tree had uncommitted changes). Reported by runners built from this repository (poot), which must give it on an 'ok' row and on a refusal ('unsupported'); absent from other engines' rows and from an 'error' row whose runner reported nothing.

build_profile.description: poot: the cargo profile the runner was built with. Only `release` is a result (the runner refuses to measure otherwise). Part of a cell's comparable identity.

build_features.description: poot: the runner's enabled cargo features, comma-separated, empty when none. Part of a cell's comparable identity.

rustc_version.description: poot: the compiler the runner was built with (`rustc --version`). Part of a cell's comparable identity.

adapter.description: poot: the adapter name the executor reported for the device it opened (not the host's first GPU). Part of a cell's comparable identity.

driver_version.description: poot: the driver stack the executor's runtime reported (Mesa/Vulkan, HSA, CUDA). Part of a cell's comparable identity.

checkpoint_digest.description: poot: blake3 over the stored weights the driver loaded (name, shape, stored dtype and bytes in key order). Two checkpoints under one model id digest differently. Part of a cell's comparable identity.

prefill_chunk.description: poot: the prefill chunk the cell ran with, in tokens: the whole longest prompt when its plan fits the device, else the largest smaller chunk that does (null in a row recorded before the field: whole prompts). Chunked and whole-prompt prefill time differently, so it is part of a cell's comparable identity; a chunk that holds the longest prompt is the whole-prompt prefill.

compute_dtype.description: poot: the dtype the engine computes in; `precision` is the dtype the weights are stored in. Part of a cell's comparable identity.

engine.description: poot: what generated the result (the driver's one loop).

driver.description: poot: the driver loop's own counters for the cell (prepared entries, retained bytes, compiles, steps, host picks, recordings and replays, and the live, peak and allocation count of its device memory by buffer role): a regression in compile or replay count shows in a stored row.

profiled.description: poot: whether the runner timed the device (`--profile`). A profiled run is a diagnostic, never throughput evidence: it is stored apart (results/diagnostics/) and compares only with another profiled run.

binary_sha256.description: poot rows: SHA-256 of the runner executable that was asked to run, read from the file by the harness; null when the runner path names no file. Names the binary; build_sha names the source it was built from. An external tool runs through an interpreter, whose digest says nothing about the tool, so its row carries framework_version instead.

family.description: The model family the poot registry resolved the checkpoint to, as the runner reports it (never a mapping from the manifest). Required on every poot 'ok' and 'unsupported' row: a string on 'ok', and on a refusal that came after the registry resolved a family; null on a refusal that came before one did (an unregistered family, a declined precision). The feature matrix joins refusals to its family rows on it.

backend.description: The backend the cell ran on (poot: ptx, rocm, wgpu or vulkan, as requested through POOT_BENCH_BACKEND and reported back by the runner; other engines: what they report, e.g. vulkan).

device.description: The accelerator the cell ran on, from the harness environment capture (env.json gpu_name); null when the host reports none. Part of a cell's identity for `bench compare`, with backend.

gen_tokens.description: Tokens generated in the timed run (fixed per scenario for comparability).

ttft_ms.description: Time to first generated token, milliseconds (median over timed iterations).

tpot_ms.description: Mean inter-token gap over decode = decode_span/(gen_tokens-1), milliseconds (median over iterations).

e2e_ms.description: End-to-end request latency, start to last token, milliseconds (median).

iterations.description: Number of timed iterations the median/stats are over.

ttft_ms_stdev.description: Stdev of TTFT across iterations (noise indicator).

peak_vram_bytes.description: Peak GPU memory used during the runner's lifetime, from the harness NVML/nvidia-smi sampler (external, uniform across frameworks). Omitted when unavailable. On an AMD GPU it is the sum of amdgpu sysfs mem_info_vram_used and mem_info_gtt_used (the GTT pool is the system memory a unified-memory APU holds), see peak_gtt_bytes.

vram_baseline_bytes.description: GPU memory used just before the runner started (other processes), subtracted is left to the report; recorded raw.

peak_gtt_bytes.description: Peak GTT (system memory mapped for the GPU) in use, from amdgpu sysfs mem_info_gtt_used; a component of peak_vram_bytes on AMD GPUs. Omitted on NVIDIA.

peak_rss_bytes.description: Peak process resident set size during the runner's lifetime, from /proc (external).

gpu_util_mean_pct.description: Mean GPU compute utilization (% of sample periods the SMs were busy) over the cell, from the external sampler. Low = headroom (idle GPU between launches/syncs).

gpu_util_peak_pct.description: Peak GPU compute utilization over the cell, from the external sampler.

cpu_util_mean_pct.description: Mean process-tree CPU utilization (%, 100% == one full core) over the cell, from psutil. Near 100% while GPU util is low points to a single-thread host bottleneck feeding the GPU.

cpu_util_peak_pct.description: Peak process-tree CPU utilization (%, 100% == one full core) over the cell.

peak_power_w.description: Peak instantaneous GPU board power draw (watts) during the runner's lifetime, from the harness sampler (NVML/nvidia-smi, or amdgpu hwmon power1_average on AMD; external, uniform across frameworks). Omitted when unavailable.

energy_j.description: Total GPU energy consumed over the cell (joules), integrated from the same power samples as peak_power_w (power_w * wall-clock dt per sample, summed). Omitted when unavailable.

energy_wh.description: energy_j converted to watt-hours (energy_j / 3600), for readability at bench-cell scale.

util_series.description: Downsampled (~1 Hz) utilization trace over the cell for plotting util-over-time. Each entry is [t_s, gpu_pct, cpu_pct, vram_bytes, rss_bytes, power_w]; spans all ISLs of a decode-curve cell (no per-ISL markers).

sampler_interval_ms.description: External sampler period; a coarse interval can miss a short-lived peak.

self_reported_vram_bytes.description: Optional: the framework's own VRAM number (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated, vLLM weight footprint, etc.) for cross-check. Not the comparison number.

osl.description: decode-curve (spec 115): the fixed output length (tokens decoded + timed) at each context length.

isl.description: decode-curve: top-level summary context length (the smallest ISL point, for the report/index headline).

curve.description: decode-curve (spec 115): one entry per requested context length (ISL), aggregated by the harness from the runner's validated raw per-token samples. Runtime validation requires exact requested ISL coverage before this row is written. The shape of decode_tok_s / tpot_ms across isl is the degradation curve.

isl.description: Context length (synthetic prefill tokens) for this point.

osl.description: Decode tokens timed at this point.

prompt_tokens.description: Tokens the runner actually prefilled; runtime validation requires it to equal isl.

iters.description: Timed iterations aggregated into this point.

ttft_ms.description: Prefill cost (start to first token), percentiles p50/p90/p99 over iters.

tpot_ms.description: Per-token decode cost = (e2e-ttft)/(osl-1), prefill EXCLUDED, percentiles p50/p90/p99.

itl_ms.description: Inter-token latency, token-weighted percentiles p50/p90/p99 over all decode gaps.

decode_tok_s.description: Steady-state decode throughput = 1000 / median tpot_ms (prefill excluded).

timing_claim.description: The timing capability the runner claims. request-window: every request reports its raw boundaries (tokens, first/last token, finish, steps) and TPOT is the mean inter-token gap; row-level: only ttft/e2e/per-token gaps are reported, TPOT is (e2e - ttft)/(osl - 1), and rows compare on the row-level identity subset only. Declared once, in harness/result_contract.py.

preparation.description: poot rows: the preparation work behind the timed window, per layer. `state` labels what the invoker declared (null when it declared none); `layers.<layer>.prepare` is the work the declared prepared set cost and `.repeat` the work repeating it added, null where no producer counts that layer (Unknown, never zero). Repeating the declared set must add no work to any layer; `open_ms` is the model load, timed apart from every request.

artifact_entries_at_start.description: Artifacts the cache directory held before the process opened anything; null when no directory was named.

caveats.description: Per-cell honesty notes: precision mismatch vs the matched target, vLLM KV-pool inflation, warmup excluded, etc. FR-009.
